title: A Normal Form for Invertible Semilinear Maps and the Category of Isocrystals Over a Finite Field
summary: For a field $L$, and a finite order automorphism $σ$, we classify invertible $σ$-semilinear endomorphisms on finite-dimensional $L$-vector spaces up to equivalence. This is deduced as a consequence of a description, in terms of certain norm equations in finite extensions of $L$, of the semilinear Schur indices for the group $\mathbb{Z}$ acting on $L$ via $σ$. As an application, we give an explicit description of the category of isocrystals over a finite field.

title: On Ext-groups between Arthur-type modules of the graded Hecke algebras of type A
summary: Let $\mathbb H_n$ be the graded Hecke algebra of type $A_{n-1}$. This article establishes a formula for Ext-groups between a Speh $\mathbb H_n$-module and a $W$-type $\mathbb H_n$-module in terms of Littlewood-Richardson coefficients. As a consequence, we obtain an explicit and efficient method to compute Ext-groups between a Speh $\mathbb H_n$-module and an Arthur-type module of $\mathbb H_n$. In particular, this proves new instances of a conjecture of Chan and Prasad on Ext non-vanishing between Arthur-type representations. We also discuss some other non-Ext vanishing results for calibrated modules.

title: Effective and explicit version of the Kazhdan - Yom-Din formula for characters of tempered representations
summary: We provide an effective expression for the character of a tempered representation in terms of its matrix coefficient. This formula is an explicit version of a formula proven in [KYD22] which generalizes Harish-Chandra's formula for characters of discrete series representations, see [HC70, Theorem 9].

title: Invariant distributions and common denominators in the Bernstein center
summary:
Let $G$ be a connected reductive group over a non-Archimedean local field. We conjecture that every invariant distribution whose support is compact modulo conjugation belongs to the rational Bernstein center. We also make an explicit conjecture about the ideal of possible denominators (the description is using a version of the local Langlands correspondence and involves working with endoscopic subgroups of $G$).
  We prove this for products of general linear groups; in this case the above idea is much more explicit and Langlands correspondence is not needed for its description (it is a principle ideal, where the generator is given by some version of the discriminant function). We also prove our general conjecture for $G=\mathrm{SL}(2)$.

title: Maximum number of cells in a matroid subdivision of hypersimplex
summary: David Speyer proved that the maximum number of cells in a regular matroid subdivision of the hypersimplex $Δ(m,t)$ is $\binom{t-2}{m-1}$ , using the language of tropical geometry and properties of the Tutte polynomial of a matroid \cite[Theorem 6.1]{Speyer}. In this paper, we prove this result in general, i.e. for arbitrary matroid subdivisions including the non-regular ones. We perform a different combinatorial way using our results in \cite{HHH} and independent of tropical language.

title: Semisimplicity of Brauer algebras associated with finite Coxeter types
summary: A finite-dimensional complex algebra is semisimple if its Jacobson radical is zero. In this paper, we determine the complex parameters for which Brauer algebras associated with finite Coxeter types are semisimple. We also determine semisimplicity at zero for the specified polynomial diagram forms and show that it can depend on the choice of polynomial form.

title: Maximal defect $2$-blocks with dihedral defect groups up to splendid Morita equivalence
summary: We classify, up to splendid Morita equivalence, all maximal defect blocks whose defect groups are dihedral \(2\)-groups of order at least \(8\). The classification holds for blocks over an algebraically closed field as well as for those over a suitable discrete valuation ring of characteristic zero. As a consequence, Puig's conjecture holds for this infinite family of blocks. Beyond the classification result itself, a central feature of the present work is the variety of methods required in its proof. Our arguments combine classical techniques of block theory with a broad range of tools and techniques that have emerged over the past twenty-five years. Amongst others these include in a crucial manner the Gorenstein-Walter classification of finite groups with dihedral Sylow \(2\)-subgroups, Linckelmann's glueing of local Morita equivalences to obtain a stable equivalence of Morita type, the modern versions of Fong's 1st and 2nd reduction theorems in terms of splendid and endo-permutation source Morita equivalences, the structure of the Dade group of endo-permutation modules, Boltje-Perepelitsky's extended theory of Brauer pairs for \(p\)-permutation modules, the fusion systems of the blocks involved, or the concrete knowledge of their decomposition matrices.

title: Higher orbifold Euler characteristics of torus representations
summary: We compute the $Γ$-Euler characteristic of a finite-dimensional representation of the compact torus $\mathbb{T}^k$ where $Γ$ is an arbitrary finitely presented group. We additionally compute the $Γ$-Euler characteristic of the unit sphere in such a representation as well as the corresponding symplectic quotient at a nonzero level of the moment map. In each case, the $Γ$-Euler characteristic is expressed in terms of the weight matrix for the representation as well as a description of the abelianization of $Γ$.

title: Flip Combinatorial Invariance for flipclasses with small residues
summary: We establish (Normal) Flip Combinatorial Invariance for flipclasses with no residues longer than 8. Actually, we show more generally that all flipclasses of finite type with no residues longer than 8 have only one increasing path. For flipclasses of Weyl type, these are precisely the flipclasses having only one increasing path. This marks a refinement of the classical Combinatorial Invariance of Kazhdan--Lusztig polynomials.

title: On representation-theoretic and homological properties of distance algebras of finite graphs
summary: Distance algebras were introduced by Asao and Ivanov to realize magnitude homology and cohomology as bigraded Tor and Ext groups. We study the representation-theoretic and homological properties of the distance algebra $Σ_G$ of a finite connected graph $G$. We characterize the graphs for which $Σ_G$ is representation-finite, multiserial, biserial, or self-injective by an explicit graph-theoretic classification. We also compute the finitistic, self-injective, and dominant dimensions for several natural families of graphs. For a finite modular lattice $L$, we consider the distance algebra $Σ_L$ associated to the Hasse graph of $L$, and show that $Σ_L$ is Auslander--Gorenstein precisely when $L$ is a finite direct product of chains. We also present a family of minimal Auslander--Gorenstein distance algebras, namely, those associated to punctured hypercubes, whose finitistic (equivalently, self-injective; equivalently, dominant) dimension can be arbitrarily large.

title: iBraid group symmetries of iquantum groups via star product
summary: We establish ibraid group symmetries on universal iquantum groups of symmetrizable Kac-Moody type, proving a conjecture of Wang and Zhang. Building on the star product realization of quantum symmetric pairs $(\widetilde{\mathbf U},\widetilde{\mathbf U}^{\imath})$, we relate these symmetries to Lusztig's braid group symmetries, extending the compatibility previously obtained via iHopf algebras in the quasi-split setting. Via the Letzter map $ψ$ from the iquantum group $\widetilde{\mathbf U}^{\imath}$ to the horospherical algebra $\mathcal A\subset \widetilde{\mathbf U}$, we show that the ibraid group symmetry $\widetilde{\mathbf T}'_{i,-1}$ of $\widetilde{\mathbf U}^{\imath}$ transported to $\mathcal A$ coincides with Lusztig's braid group symmetry $\widetilde T_{\mathbf r_i}^{-1}$ on the subalgebra $\mathcal R_{\bullet,i}^{-,r}$. Finally, a mixed product formula, together with a parabolic decomposition, yields an explicit formula for the transported action on the entire horospherical algebra $\mathcal A$.

title: Algebraic Vector Fields on Compact Homogeneous Spaces are 2-generated
summary: Let $M$ be a compact, connected manifold on which a compact Lie group $K$ acts smoothly and transitively. We show that the Lie algebra of algebraic vector fields on $M$, i.e., of smooth vector fields whose translates under $K$ span finite-dimensional spaces, is generated by two vector fields. Consequently, the subgroup generated by the flows of these two vector fields is dense in the identity component of the diffeomorphism group of $M$. For spheres, explicit generators are obtained from earlier results on spherical vector fields.

title: Positivity in symmetric webs and block permanents
comment: 31 pages, many figures, Lean verification available, comments welcome
summary: We use symmetric webs to prove Marcus's block-permanent inequality for up to four blocks of every size, for five blocks of size at least three, and for any fixed number of blocks above an explicit logarithmic bound on the block size. The proof idea is easy: Bending strands in the Schur relation turns the comparison into a calculation with squared norms.

title: Exotic cluster structures on $Sp_{2n}$
summary: We modify the seeds of Berenstein, Fomin and Zelevinsky attached to reduced words for~$(w_0,w_0)$, for any simply connected simple complex algebraic group and any aperiodic Belavin--Drinfeld pair. In every type, moves of words act on the resulting seeds by mutations. After a change of coordinates introduced by Gekhtman, Shapiro and Vainshtein, the seeds are, for $SL_N$, seeds of the cluster structures of these authors, and for $Sp_{2n}$ they define regular complete cluster structures with the expected properties. This proves the aperiodic version of their conjecture for $Sp_{2n}$, with its uniqueness part in a refined form.

title: The BMM symmetrising trace conjecture for all exceptional complex reflection groups
summary: We prove the symmetrising trace conjecture of Broué, Malle and Michel for the generic Hecke algebras of all exceptional complex reflection groups. A key ingredient is a new family of bases, constructed via breadth-first search, which generalise the standard basis of an Iwahori-Hecke algebra. These bases provide a uniform proof of the freeness conjecture of Broué, Malle and Rouquier for these groups. The verification for each group reduces to a finite computation, carried out using programs developed with the assistance of a large language model.

title: Quantum $K$-theoretic Whitney relation for Lagrangian Grassmannian
summary: We give a quantum $K$-theoretic analogue of the Whitney relation for the torus-equivariant $K$-ring of the Lagrangian Grassmannian. As a consequence, we give a presentation of the torus-equivariant quantum $K$-ring of the Lagrangian Grassmannian. The strategy for obtaining such relations is to use the quantum $K$-theoretic Whitney relation for the full-flag manifold in type $C$ established by the author and Kato's pushforward map from the quantum $K$-ring of the full-flag manifold to that of the partial flag manifold. Then the Nakayama-type argument established by Gu et al., together with the classical Whitney presentation for the torus-equivariant $K$-ring of the Lagrangian Grassmannian, gives a proof of such a presentation.

title: Generic unipotent representations of finite reductive groups
summary: Let $\mathbb{G}$ be a generic reductive group in the sense of Broué--Malle--Michel. We construct a category over $\mathbb{Z}[t,t^{-1}]$ which interpolates between the various categories of unipotent representations of $\mathbb{G}(q)$ as we specialize $t$ to $q$. We use this category to show two properties of the unipotent decomposition matrix of $\mathbb{G}(q)$ mod $\ell$ (not dividing $q$): that, uniformly in $(q,\ell)$, there are finitely many such matrices and that for $\ell$ large enough, depending only on $\mathbb{G}$, this decomposition matrix depends only on the root of unity corresponding to $q$ mod $\ell$. We also prove that for $q$ and $q'$ two prime powers that are $\ell$-adically close enough, the categories of unipotent mod $\ell$ representations of $\mathbb{G}(q)$ and $\mathbb{G}(q')$ are equivalent.

title: The cohomology of finite simple groups is unbounded
summary: In every fixed positive degree, we show that the cohomology of finite simple groups, algebraic groups and quantum groups, with coefficients in simple modules, can have arbitrarily large dimension. In particular, we disprove Guralnick's conjecture.

title: Parahoric Spherical Whittaker Functions
summary: Let $F$ be a non-archimedean local field and let $K_μ$ be a standard parahoric subgroup of $GL_n(F)$. We express the diagonal values of normalized parahoric Whittaker eigenfunctions with trivial central character using blockwise Casselman--Shalika formulas with the appropriate modulus factor. Every irreducible generic Iwahori-spherical representation has a one-dimensional fixed space for a suitable parahoric, with no invariants under a strictly larger parahoric. The full Hecke character of this line determines the representation. We compute its adjacent-block Hecke eigenvalues and, under additional irreducibility hypotheses, obtain an explicit finite formula on every Bruhat cell using an opposite induced model, Whittaker-preserving intertwiners, and Demazure--Whittaker operators. We apply these formulas to local Rankin--Selberg integrals for $GL_n\times GL_1$ and for compatible parahorics in $GL_n\times GL_m$. In the latter case, the lowest Laurent coefficient and the equal-rank functional equation determine the integral. Explicit translations and rescalings then give test vectors for the local $L$-factor.

title: Finite-dimensional irreducible representations of Yangians
comment: 9 pages with Appendix, minor revisions, the Appendix was shortened
summary: We present a direct proof of the well-known classification of finite-dimensional representations of the Yangian $Y(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ following an approach by Chary-Pressley for $U_q(\mathfrak{ \hat sl_2})$.

title: The 3-adic Steinberg block and a categorical 3-adic local Langlands correspondence for $\text{GL}_2(\mathbb{Q}_3)$
summary: We extend the work of Johansson-Newton-Wang-Erickson on a categorical $p$-adic Langlands correspondence over $\text{GL}_2(\mathbb{Q}_p)$ to $p = 3$ by recontextualizing their construction in the Steinberg case. We produce a novel, more categorical method of analyzing the properties of this construction without requiring an explicit algebraic presentation. As input to this argument, we also perform some new analysis of the representation theory of the $3$-adic Steinberg block of $\text{GL}_2(\mathbb{Q}_3)$, obtaining results complementing those of Paškūnas.

title: Symplectic extension graphs and Ribet's lemma
summary: Let $p$ be an odd prime, and let $ρ\colon G\to \mathrm{GSp}_{2n}(\mathbb Z_p)$ be an irreducible symplectic residually multiplicity-free representation. We define the symplectic extension graph $Γ_ρ^{\mathrm{GSp}}$ associated with $ρ$ to be the directed graph whose vertices are the residual factors of $ρ$ and a directed edge between two vertices corresponds to a nonsplit extension between the vertices realized by a $G$-stable symplectic lattice. Using the Euclidean Bruhat--Tits building associated with $\mathrm{GSp}_{2n}(\mathbb Q_p)$, we prove, under suitable assumptions, the existence of certain paths in $Γ_ρ^{\mathrm{GSp}}$ and show that $Γ_ρ^{\mathrm{GSp}}$ is a disjoint union of nonempty strongly connected subgraphs. Moreover, we provide examples to show that the result we obtain is optimal.

title: Koszul duality for finite-dimensional Koszul algebras
comment: 25 pages. This paper continues A Non-graded Koszul Duality and Its Applications and merges two preprints. Most results date from 2018 to 2020, extending Bautista and Liu's work to quadratic monomial algebras. Recently, we used the homological perturbation lemma to extract homological information about Koszul dual algebras. All results are the author's own; no AI tools were used in the research
summary: Let $\La$ be a finite-dimensional Koszul algebra with Koszul dual $\Ld$. Using the Koszul functors and the homological perturbation lemma, we describe the minimal projective resolution of every object of the bounded derived category of finite-dimensional graded $\La$-modules in terms of the cohomology of the corresponding complex of coperfect graded $\Ld$-modules. In particular, the linear part of the minimal graded projective resolution of a finite-dimensional graded $\La$-module is a direct sum of Koszul complexes of these cohomology modules. We deduce that $\La$ is absolutely Koszul if and only if $\Ld$ is graded left co-coherent, if and only if the category of coperfect graded $\Ld$-modules is abelian. As applications, we show that absolutely Koszul algebras of finite global linearity defect have finite graded finitistic dimension; we refine the graded and ungraded Koszul dualities and construct nonstandard $t$-structures on the bounded derived and singularity categories. Finally, we apply these results to finite-dimensional quadratic monomial algebras.

title: Extremely proximal actions and primitivity of group rings
comment: v2: Major changes. The main theorem in the previous version should be considered retracted. See Remark 2.2
summary: We present a purely dynamical criterion for the primitivity of group rings. To be precise, we show that if $G$ is a countable group that admits a topologically free, extremely proximal action, then the group ring $KG$ is primitive for any field $K$. Our criterion recovers several of the existing results on primitivity and applies to new examples, such as the commensurator groups of torsion-free non-elementary hyperbolic groups, some Kac-Moody groups, and other weakly hyperbolic groups.

title: A conjecture on the action of Hecke operators
summary:
Let $F$ be a non-Archimedean local field of characteristic different from $2$ and $E/F$ be a quadratic étale algebra.
  For a central division $F$-algebras $L$ of a fixed degree $n$ we identify the double quotients of the homogeneous spaces $L_E^\times/L^\times$ with a topological space $Ξ_E$ which does not depend on a choice of $L$ , define a convolution products $\ast _L$ on the space ${\mathcal M} _E$ compactly supported measures on $Ξ_E$ and conjecture that the product $\ast _L$ on $Ξ_E$ does not depend on a choice of $L$.

title: Functional Compression as Occam's Razor: Algebraic Complexity from Sensitivity Minimization
comment: 28 pages, 3 figures. Version 5: major revision, adding results for arbitrary binary operations, positive-gap theorems, and Lean 4 formalizations of the main theoretical results
summary: Discovering discrete algebraic structures from data is a fundamental challenge in machine learning. We ask how continuous learning objectives can favor functional compression---representing data through shared algebraic composition rather than low-rank representations. We analyze the global optima of a canonical factorization model for algebraic completion (recovering finite binary operations) that demonstrated a preference for group operations. We measure algebraic complexity by the infimum of parameter sensitivity under exact reconstruction. We establish a universal complexity floor, whose attainment forces geometric alignment and unitarity of the latent representations. At the floor, input representations compose into the corresponding output representations; their reuse across the operation table propagates these local identities to enforce a globally shared algebraic structure. If the floor is not attained, a positive gap separates it from the feasible infimum. For cancellative operations, floor attainment forces the model's latent representation to be an injective homomorphism, equivalent to the target being isotopic to a group. In this case, every global minimizer is equivalent to the underlying group's unitary left-regular representation, up to isotopy and unitary gauge, resolving the central conjecture of Huh (2025). For non-cancellative operations, floor attainment forces exact structural redundancies (identical rows or columns) and is equivalent to a unitary factorization of the target's row- and column-reduced table with orthonormal output matrices, yielding the fewest distinct input matrices compatible with exact reconstruction. The resulting cancellative table then embeds in a group-isotope table. This analysis reveals a structural bias toward functional compression: at the sensitivity floor, algebraic composition of latent representations implements the target operation.

title: Virasoro elements in conformal algebras
comment: 24 pages; title changed, Theorem 3.3 updated, added the proof of Lemma 5.2, to appear in Communications in Mathematical Physics
summary: It is well known that Virasoro elements play an extremely important role in the theory of vertex operator algebras, and likewise a very significant role in the field of conformal algebras. In this paper, we introduce the notion of a regular action in the category of conformal modules over Lie conformal algebras with Virasoro elements. We show that a finite conformal module over the general conformal algebra $\mathfrak{gc}_1$ (resp., $\mathfrak{gc}_N$ with $N\ge2$) is semisimple if and only if there exists a pair of different Virasoro elements (resp., canonical Virasoro elements) with regular actions. Along the way to finding semisimplicity criteria, we also discuss the classification of Virasoro elements of $\mathfrak{gc}_N$ in-depth, leading us to construct a huge number of new Virasoro conformal modules.

title: Non-commutative crepant resolutions of toric singularities with divisor class group of rank one
summary:
We classify the basic reflexive modules giving toric non-commutative crepant resolutions (NCCRs) of Gorenstein toric singularities whose divisor class group has rank one. Their isomorphism classes are parametrized by nonempty proper upper sets in a partially ordered quotient of the class group. Each upper set determines a finite subset called its window, which specifies the divisorial summands. The number of summands in each such module equals the normalized volume of the associated lattice polytope, as conjectured by Van den Bergh. If two upper sets differ by one element, their modules are related by a finite sequence of Iyama--Wemyss mutations. Such sequences connect any two of the classified modules, so all toric NCCRs of a fixed singularity are derived equivalent.
  We construct higher-dimensional analogues of dimer dual quivers when the associated $d$-dimensional lattice polytope is non-pyramidal. The same window determines a cut of a periodic quiver on the $d$-torus. The cut gives an explicit presentation of the endomorphism algebra by a quiver with relations. For $d=2$, the resulting quiver is dual to a dimer model, a bipartite tiling of the two-torus.

title: On a tamely ramified local relative Langlands conjecture via categorical representations
comment: 47 pages, in comparison to previous version: proof of main theorem is slightly modified, a new supplement result (Theorem 1.3) addressing generation by one element in the unramified relative local Langlands conjecture, and a case study (Section 7) is described in details
summary: Let $G$ be a complex reductive group. For a smooth affine spherical $G$-variety $X$ such that the stabilizer of a point in the $B$-orbit under the $B$-action be connected, assume that the unramified relative local Langlands conjecture of Ben-Zvi-Sakellaridis-Venkatesh (BZSV) for $X$ holds. We establish a spectral description of a full subcategory of Iwahori equivariant coherent D-modules on $LX$ in terms of the relative Langlands dual of $X$, confirming a tamely ramified local relative Langlands conjecture proposed by Devalapurkar.

title: Equivalence Relations on Vertex Operator Algebras, II: Witt Equivalence and Orbifolds
comment: 80 pages, 17 figures, LaTeX; minor improvements; to appear in Ann. Henri Poincaré
summary:
When can two strongly rational vertex operator algebras or 1+1d rational conformal field theories (RCFTs) be related by topological manipulations? For vertex operator algebras, the term "topological manipulations" refers to operations like passing to a conformal extension or restricting to a conformal subalgebra; for RCFTs, topological manipulations include operations like gauging (or orbifolding) a finite part of a generalized global symmetry or interpolating to a new theory via a topological line interface of finite quantum dimension.
  Inspired by results in the theory of even lattices and tensor categories, we say that two strongly rational vertex operator algebras are Witt equivalent if their central charges agree and if their modular tensor categories are Witt equivalent. Two RCFTs are said to be Witt equivalent if their central charges agree and if their associated 2+1d topological field theories can be separated by a topological surface. We argue that Witt equivalence is necessary for two theories to be related by topological manipulations. We conjecture that it is also sufficient, and give proofs in various special cases.
  We relate this circle of ideas to the problem of classifying RCFTs, and to lore concerning deformation classes of quantum field theories. We use the notion of Witt equivalence to argue, conditional on a mild technical hypothesis, that all of the finite symmetries of the $\mathrm{SU}(2)_1$ Wess-Zumino-Witten model are invertible. We also sketch a "quantum Galois theory" for chiral CFTs, which generalizes prior mathematical literature by incorporating non-invertible symmetries; we illustrate this non-invertible Galois theory in the context of the monster CFT $V^\natural$, for which we produce two Fibonacci lines. Finally, we discuss $p$-neighborhood of vertex operator algebras, which is a special topological manipulation related to $\mathbb{Z}_p$-orbifolding.
